Notes: wRC+ and all baselines are division-relative, so cross-division matchups grade each player against his own league. Hand splits and batted-ball data come from pitch-tracked PAs; most players get real vs-LHP/vs-RHP (and vs-LHB/vs-RHB) splits reconstructed from 2023-2026 per-PA play-by-play, bucketed by the opponent's actual handedness, where 8+ PA (hitters) / 10+ PA (pitchers) per side exist; the rest fall back to season-line estimates (marked est) with a league-default platoon adjustment. Rosters: top hitters by PA; top 4 starters by innings + top 4 relievers ranked saves-first, so closers qualify by role. Source: nwbaseballstats.com API, 2026 season snapshot.

Matchup Score Formula

The favorability score (1-10) is computed using a weighted Bayesian approach:

Score = 50% × OverallQuality + 35% × SplitPerformance + 15% × RecentForm (weights follow sample reliability)

After weighting, the deviation from neutral (5.0) is amplified by 1.15× to spread matchup differences across the full 1-10 range visibly, then clamped to [1, 10]. This scaling is presentation only; the underlying leg calculations (each normalized to ±5) are unchanged.

Bayesian Shrinkage

Splits shrink toward the player's own season rate (a large, reliable sample), not a flat league constant. For relievers, the prior sample size is reduced to match their smaller role volumes (20 IP for overall, 8 IP for recent form) compared to starters (50 IP / 15 IP):

wRC+_split_adj = (PA_split × wRC+_split + 200 × wRC+_season) / (PA_split + 200)

For pitchers: FIP_split_adj = (IP_split × FIP_split + Prior_IP × FIP_season) / (IP_split + Prior_IP)

Season and Recent-form totals shrink toward league average (200 PA / 50 IP prior), since there's no larger real sample to anchor to at that level. Recent additionally shrinks toward the player's own season-adjusted number (30 PA / 15 IP prior) rather than raw recent numbers, since recent windows are too small to trust directly.

Log5 Outcome Probability Model

Outcome probabilities use Bill James' Log5 method, adapted for batter-pitcher matchups:

π = (B × P / L) / [(B × P / L) + ((1-B) × (1-P) / (1-L))]

Where B = batter rate, P = pitcher rate, L = league average. Applied to: Hit, Walk, Strikeout, and Out probabilities.

Platoon Handling

Real hand splits (pitch-tracked PAs) are shrunk toward the player's season line. Placeholder splits (untracked players) get a league-default platoon adjustment instead: same-hand ~-4% for the hitter, opposite-hand ~+3%. Switch hitters always take the platoon advantage.

Head-to-Head History (BvP)

Where two selected players have 3+ real plate appearances against each other (parsed from NWAC and NCAA play-by-play logs, 2023-2026), the actual results are shown above the player cards. By design this is context only and never feeds the matchup score: college BvP samples are far too small to be predictive, and the shrinkage framework would discount them to near-zero anyway.

Projected PA Line & Confidence

The projected AVG/OBP/SLG/xwOBA is computed from the same per-PA outcome tree using linear weights (0.69 BB, 0.89 1B, 1.27 2B, 1.62 3B, 2.10 HR). The confidence chip grades the sample behind the score: season PA/IP volume plus whether each side's hand split is tracked or estimated.

References: FanGraphs wRC+ | FanGraphs FIP | PMC - Bayesian Hierarchical Log5
